c.h: A vision (the editors suggest it may relate to Peter)
v: ‘... overcame me. And Jesus stood by in a vision and said, Why art thou cast down? For it is not thou who ... but he who gave (?) ...’
‘... thou didst say ..., making no answer. What then hast thou forbidden? What is the new doctrine that they say thou teachest, or what the new baptism that thou dost preach? Answer and ...’

‘The scribes and Pharisees and priests seeing him had indignation because he reclined in the midst of sinners. And Jesus hearing them said, They that are whole need not a physician, [but they that are sick].’
‘... and pray for your enemies; for he that is not against you is with you. He that to-day is afar off shall to-morrow be near you, and in ... of the adversary ...’

credit: P.Oxy. X 1224 (“Uncanonical Gospel”, 4th century), translated by Bernard P. Grenfell and Arthur S. Hunt, The Oxyrhynchus Papyri, Part X (London: Egypt Exploration Fund, 1914), pp. 1–10. Public domain. Scan: archive.org/details/oxyrhynchuspapyr10gren. Order of the pages as the editors print them (they discuss whether recto ii precedes verso i). Square brackets are the editors’ restorations; “...” marks gaps in the papyrus. Fragment 1 is too broken for the editors to translate and is omitted. OCR fixes: “Answerand” → “Answer and”, “andin” → “and in”.
